Q: Is there a way to give Device Owner Permission in app without running it in Kiosk Mode? A:

Yes, Device Owner and Kiosk Mode are separate concepts. A Device Owner app can use enterprise management APIs without ever enabling Lock Task (kiosk) mode. Lock Task Mode is optional and only activated if your app explicitly calls the relevant APIs. Many EMM/MDM solutions run as Device Owner while still allowing normal access to the launcher, settings, and other applications.

For provisioning, the app must be installed on a freshly factory-reset device (or during enterprise enrollment) and then set as Device Owner. For testing, the typical ADB command is:

adb shell dpm set-device-owner your.package.name/.YourDeviceAdminReceiver

This only works if no accounts are configured and the device is in a state that permits Device Owner assignment. On production devices, provisioning is usually done via QR code, NFC, zero-touch enrollment, or Android Enterprise enrollment flows rather than ADB.

Regarding silent installs and downgrades, being Device Owner alone is not sufficient to bypass all package-management restrictions. You can perform silent installs using PackageInstaller, but version downgrades require explicit downgrade support. With PackageInstaller.SessionParams, Android provides:

params.setRequestDowngrade(true);

(or SessionParams.REQUEST_DOWNGRADE on older API variants).

However, the downgrade will still only succeed if the platform version supports it and the caller has the required privileges. In practice, support varies across Android versions and OEM implementations. Even as Device Owner, you cannot universally force arbitrary APK downgrades on every non-rooted device. Testing on the exact Android version and device family you intend to support is essential because enterprise APIs and package-install behavior are not perfectly consistent across vendors.

Q: How can I replace backward slash to forward slash using Java? A:

The String.replace(CharSequence, CharSequence) example provided by Paul and by Bohemian will work, but it’s better to use the String.replace(char, char) version.

It is slightly faster. Though you won't have a noticeable speed difference, it’s better to do such optimisations where possible.

String replacedStr = str.replace('\\', '/');

Q: Does Rust memory safety provide correctness assurance similar to Ada type safety? A:

Both provide similar safety guarantees. However Ada, in many cases does this through runtime checks (e.g. vectors).

Q: ResourceExhausted: 429 with "limit: 0" on Gemini API Free Tier (LangChain) even after new project A:

Its because you aren't connected to the API properly. In Gemini CLI after quitting it shows Total Quota Used, If it shows 0 for everything...you aren't connected.
This is a problem I faced when using it through Docker Container.

Here's the docker-compose.yml file to fix that (make sure to update docker desktop to latest version) :

services:
  # --- GEMINI 3 (LATEST) ---
  
  # BEST DAILY DRIVER: Smart, Fast, Free
  flash3:
    image: us-docker.pkg.dev/gemini-code-dev/gemini-cli/sandbox:0.1.1
    environment:
      - GEMINI_API_KEY=${GEMINI_API_KEY}
      - GEMINI_NO_INDEX=true
    ports:
      - "8100-8110:8000-8010"  # Web Preview Port Range (Adjust as needed for tools) (Currently accessible via localhost:8100, 8101, etc.)
    volumes: &vols
      - D:\Projects\Gemini-CLI-Projects\All-Projects:/app/workspace
      - ./gemini_config:/home/node/.gemini
      - ./GEMINI.md:/home/node/GEMINI.md:ro
      - ./Global-Docs:/app/library:ro
    command: gemini -m gemini-3-flash-preview
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

also make a .env file, Edit it and add this 1 line :

GEMINI_API_KEY=your_actual_api_key_here

Put your api key instead of "your_actual_api_key_here".

Now go to the Folder where docker-compose.yml is and open cmd > Then paste this line and hit enter : docker compose run --rm flash3.

Make Sure Docker Engine is Running🙂
